construct: RULED, THE K2 CELL (refreshed 2026-09-21): k2_overview 40–70w (the persona's current in the element's arena) + k2_functional ≤22w (the god's own family function, re-ruled 2026-09-01) + k2_domain_readings 18–55w per ruled domain (owner construct 2026-08-19, corpus ×50 LOCKED) · adj_chips {catalyst ×3, friction ×3} 1–3w under THE KEYWORD DERIVATION CHAIN (2026-09-03) and THE VOCABULARY ZONE B1–B2 (2026-09-04) · fn_reading = the weighted three-door ledger {word, doors:{trait, scene, outside}} ×3 per pole, 35–55w per door (THE THREE DOORS 2026-09-03; corpus ×50 complete 2026-09-04) · structural_interaction = the REA_03 §4b authoring seed · k2_card = the unauthored register stub (REA_03 §4, superseded by the cell above). Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Water directing Fire broadly — depth ranging across warmth as distributed material
candidates.k2_overview: Your Fire moves as the Horizon: light that spends itself gladly. Opportunity finds you at gatherings, luck likes your laugh, and money arrives in blazes and leaves by the same door. You are fortune’s favorite dinner guest. Learn to pocket the bread, and the feast never really ends.
candidates.k2_functional: You seize chances at speed, brilliant in windows, bored in pipelines.

k2_domain_readings.Opportunity: Chances come to you socially: the tip at the table, the partner met at the party. Keep circulating, it is genuinely your economy. Just write things down before the candles burn out.
k2_domain_readings.Ventures: Your ventures shine at launch: openings, campaigns, anything with a lit fuse and a crowd. Pair every firework with a caretaker who loves the quiet part. That partnership is your fortune.
k2_domain_readings.Father: The father-thread flickers warm and irregular: a paternal figure of charisma, generosity, or absence in flares. You inherited the shine and the volatility. Spend the first, insure against the second.

angles.drive: You see chances early, at their smallest. Being first matters to you more than being sure, and you move while the chance is only a guess. If you name what you see early, the credit stays yours when it pays.
angles.cost_self: Your eye goes to the far chance before the near one. You look ahead for the next opening more than down at what is in hand. Check what is already yours first, and you stop losing the nearest chance to the far one.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you see a new chance, you bring it to your partners before the last one pays. You would rather share the next idea than finish the current plan. Once you hand them the finished thing, you keep them for the one after.

angles.drive: Giving comes easily to you, often before you have counted. Generosity is how you feel rich, so you would rather give the thing now than keep it for a tighter month. Keep giving as you do, and note what each gift costs you.
angles.cost_self: Giving easily leaves little behind for you. You want the pleasure of giving now more than a cushion later, and now keeps winning. When you set aside the price of one gift each month, you fund the venture you keep giving away.
angles.cost_others: You give in big moments rather than small steady ways. Being generous feels truer to you than being careful, and your family gets the big day and lives through the gap. With small gifts that repeat, you give them the steadiness along with the shine.

angles.drive: In a new venture, you start fast and plan later. The beginning is the warm part, and you would rather open the next one than sit through the middle. When you start fast on fewer ventures, you get to know the ones you start.
angles.cost_self: The easy part for you is the start. You would rather start something new than wait out a long middle, so most ventures end where the rush does. If each fast start must prove itself after the rush, you lose only the weak ventures.
angles.cost_others: You start at full speed, with your partners pulled in beside you. Being at the beginning suits you more than staying for the middle, and the long part lands on them. Name your part before you start, so you ask less of their patience.

angles.drive: The newest thing is what you want. Because new things wake you up, a fresh chance pulls you more than a half-done one holds you. With each chase, you trade away the catch already in your hands, the only one you were sure of.
angles.cost_self: Chasing the new keeps you at the start. Each new chance looks better than the one in hand, so you leave before it pays back. Each time you leave early, you lose the money at the end, and that money is why you chase.
angles.cost_others: Whenever something new shows up, you chase it and leave your partners the middle. You want the next chance more than the ending of this one, since staying put feels like falling behind. Do not forget that every chase costs them the ending you promised.

angles.drive: Spending fast is your reflex. Money is only real to you once it is used, so you spend it now instead of saving it. You enjoy each purchase and meet the next lean month with nothing saved.
angles.cost_self: Fast spending feels like freedom to you. You would rather have the thing now than the money later, and what comes in easily goes before it grows. You never build the stake a venture of your own would need.
angles.cost_others: You spend shared money fast, often before you ask. You put spending on your own call ahead of deciding together, so you hand your family a choice already made. You take their say with each fast spend, and asking first gives it back.

angles.drive: Looking past home comes easily to you. The next venture feels like where your life begins, so you look ahead at what might come rather than at what is here. You are already living the life you look past.
angles.cost_self: Whenever you look past home, you save your best for what comes next. You would rather look toward somewhere new than settle where you already are. You miss the rest your own home was built to give you.
angles.cost_others: You look past the people at home first. Getting to the next venture matters more to you than being with them, so you give them what is left. You lose almost nothing by giving them the first look instead of the last.

edge.lead: Fire runs through your wealth, your family and your social life. It is the chance you spot while it is still small and cheap, the home that always makes space for another chair, and the stranger who is a friend before the evening ends.
